actual: Read the full controlling TeX and all four actual PDF pages as text and rendered visuals.
proof: For the bilinear annihilator of the full holomorphic L¹ class on the unit disk, the bounded angular input ρ has Bρ=1+log|z|² on the punctured disk under the stipulated negative-kernel principal value, so its essential norm is unbounded. For every m≥1 a displayed polynomial v_m has unit essential input norm and transform norm exactly H_m. Zero extension yields exterior transform zero almost everywhere.

Full annihilation uses the angular exponent 2 and circle Taylor convergence under absolute-integrability Fubini, for any analytic L¹ test. The absolutely-integrable Cauchy potential produces the exact mode formula and zero exterior with no holomorphic correction. Distributional integration by parts gives the normalized kernels; local subtraction of the value yields pointwise PV away from the singularities, and the origin of the logarithmic example has the specified divergent PV.

The zero boundary trace and inner r² log r bound rule out point or boundary contributions. The radial polynomial transform increases from −H_m to 1, and the continuous approach on disks of positive area gives the true essential supremum including m=1. No common polynomial constant does not assert an unbounded output of an individual polynomial.
